subtopics.title: Energy, the Joule, and Energy Stored by Position

questions.question: Gravitational potential energy is energy stored because of an object's:
In E_p = mgh, the product m × g represents:
options: The object's weight — the force gravity exerts on it

questions.question: One joule is roughly the effort of:
options: Lifting a small apple through one metre
Lifting a brick to a rooftop

questions.question: Energy is a scalar quantity, which means an energy answer:
options: Has size only — joules never point anywhere

subtopics.title: Pricing the Lift — 2 Kilograms to 5 Metres

questions.question: For the 2 kg brick lifted 5 m (g = 9,8 m/s²), the potential energy gained is:
The unit check works because kg × m/s² gives newtons, and newtons × metres give:
options: Joules — a newton-metre is exactly a joule

questions.question: The further gain from the 5 m platform to the 12 m platform can be computed as 235,2 − 98, or directly as:
options: 2 × 9,8 × 7 — pricing only the 7 m height difference

questions.question: Both roads give 137,2 J because changes in potential energy depend only on:
options: The total height above sea level
The path taken by the brick

subtopics.title: The Reference Level — Where Zero Lives

questions.question: The ground observer says the brick has 98 J; the basement observer, 3 m lower, says 156,8 J. Who is correct?
options: Both — each is correct relative to its own declared reference level
Neither — the reference level must be sea level

questions.question: Physics tolerates different zero choices because nature only ever cashes in:
options: Energy differences — which agree whatever zero was chosen

questions.question: An object below your chosen reference level has:
options: Negative potential energy — legitimately less than at zero

questions.question: The forbidden move with reference levels is:
options: Mixing two different zeros inside one problem
Choosing the lowest point as zero
Declaring the zero in the first line

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: A question supplies a WEIGHT of 19,6 N. Before using E_p = mgh you must:
options: Multiply the 19,6 by g to be safe
Divide by g to recover the mass of 2 kg — weight is not mass
Convert the weight to joules first

questions.question: A trolley is pushed 10 m up a ramp that rises 3 m vertically. The h in E_p = mgh is:
options: 3 m — only the vertical height counts

questions.question: A 500 g ball raised 250 cm has E_p equal to:
This formula matters for the next lessons because:
options: It replaces the equations of motion entirely
It only appears again in Grade 12 chemistry
Potential energy is the last energy topic in CAPS
Stored E_p converts to kinetic energy, and conservation of mechanical energy links the two

subtopics.title: The Bank Account in the Sky

questions.question: In the water-tower picture, pumping water up at night is:
options: A deposit — work banked as potential energy in the raised water
A way to cool the water

questions.question: The 'lifting bill' reads E_p = mgh in two halves:
options: Mass times height, then times speed
Weight (m × g) times the height lifted — force times distance
Height times g, divided by mass

questions.question: The stored energy 'pays out' when:
options: The object falls — height converts back to speed

questions.question: Which change increases the deposit the MOST for a lifted object?
options: Halving the mass and doubling the height
Doubling the mass and halving the height
Keeping mass and height, lifting faster
Doubling both the mass and the height — the bill multiplies by four

questions.question: The brick's weight, used as the per-metre charge, is:
The top-up from 5 m to 12 m costs 137,2 J by both roads because:
options: Gravity charges per metre climbed, so only the height change matters
The two roads round differently to the same answer
The brick becomes lighter higher up

questions.question: The brick's full balance on the 12 m platform, measured from the ground, is:
Building sites require hard hats because a falling brick:
options: Loses its energy harmlessly to the air
Pays out its full banked potential energy as speed on the way down

questions.question: Heights have no natural zero, so the reference level is:
options: Your free choice — declared once and used throughout

questions.question: The two bookkeepers disagree on the brick's balance but agree on the 98 J released in the fall because:
options: The basement observer corrected an error
Their zero-point disagreement subtracts away in the difference
The fall changes the reference level
Energy is only real at ground level

questions.question: Choosing the lowest point of a problem as the zero is recommended because:
options: It makes every height positive and the arithmetic friendly
It is the only physically correct choice

questions.question: An object below your chosen zero is described in account language as:
options: Bankrupt, with no energy at all
Overdrawn — a negative balance the mathematics handles without complaint
